assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made the strong, controllable interaction of single artificial atoms and microwave photons a practical physical regime, with profound consequences for quantum optics and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Girvin provided decisive theoretical architecture, while Schoelkopf established its experimental power; Andreas Wallraff is also central to the experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena and platform have been reproduced and extended broadly over two decades, making the discovery fully mature.
uncertainties: The conceptual and experimental credit is unusually distributed, and a three-person award cannot represent all central contributors.
Its boundary relative to the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits would require especially careful definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their theoretical blueprint for trapped-ion quantum computing and quantum simulation transformed controllable atomic systems into a general laboratory for quantum many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear joint originators of the influential foundational proposals.
assessment.maturity: The underlying ideas have been realized in many laboratories and now underpin a substantial experimental field.
uncertainties: The achievement is principally theoretical and overlaps conceptually with broader quantum-information contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade created a strikingly clean route to programmable, strongly interacting quantum systems and opened a new experimental regime for quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: Saffman's theoretical work and the Lukin and Browaeys experimental programmes are central, though Grangier also made important foundational contributions.
assessment.maturity: Large, coherent neutral-atom arrays and blockade-mediated operations are now robustly demonstrated across laboratories.
uncertainties: The most appropriate division between early blockade physics and later programmable-array development needs careful historical assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction supplied the essential physical logic by which fragile quantum states can in principle support reliable computation, a fundamental conceptual breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Shor, Kitaev, and Steane each made distinct foundational contributions to codes and fault-tolerant architectures.
assessment.maturity: Core principles are experimentally established and early logical demonstrations are compelling, although full-scale fault tolerance remains ahead.
uncertainties: Whether present experimental realization is sufficiently mature for a prize centered on fault-tolerant computation remains uncertain.
Many further contributors were indispensable to the broader field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and geometric phase revealed that phase and gauge structure have directly observable physical consequences, reshaping modern quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov is directly identified with the first effect and Berry with the latter; both contributions have distinct, exceptional conceptual clarity.
assessment.maturity: Both effects are long-established experimentally and have become standard tools across quantum physics.
uncertainties: The two discoveries are related through phase and topology but are historically distinct, making their treatment as one prize question less straightforward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks achieved an extraordinary synthesis of quantum control and precision measurement, creating clocks of unprecedented accuracy and scientific reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept, while Ye made defining experimental advances and expanded its precision frontier.
assessment.maturity: Independent implementations have reached exceptional reproducibility and support demanding tests and measurements.
uncertainties: The precise balance of conceptual origin and subsequent experimental development requires careful attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned quantum measurement and entanglement into an operationally new form of secure communication, helping establish quantum information as a physical discipline.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced the foundational protocol, and Ekert gave the entanglement-based formulation of comparable conceptual importance.
assessment.maturity: The central protocols are repeatedly demonstrated and deployed, with their physical principles firmly established.
uncertainties: Practical security depends on implementation details beyond the ideal protocols.
The intellectual territory substantially overlaps with other foundational quantum-information achievements.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry made matter-wave coherence into a precise and versatile measurement instrument, enabling major advances in inertial sensing and tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard, and Kasevich made major complementary theoretical and experimental contributions to its emergence.
assessment.maturity: The methods are well established, widely replicated, and continue to set precision benchmarks.
uncertainties: The field has many foundational contributors, so limiting recognition to three names is difficult.
Its most decisive scientific discovery is less sharply bounded than for some higher-ranked candidates.
